## Purpose

This procedure describes the determination of dissolved organic carbon
(DOC) in natural water samples (surface water, groundwater,
stormwater, treated effluent) by the non-purgeable organic carbon
(NPOC) method on the Shimadzu TOC-L analyzer. DOC is a fundamental
water quality parameter that influences aquatic ecosystem productivity,
light penetration, metal complexation, disinfection byproduct
formation, and nutrient cycling [@thurman1985; @wetzel2001].

The NPOC method acidifies the sample and sparges with carrier gas to
remove inorganic carbon (CO~2~, HCO~3~^-^, CO~3~^2-^) before
combustion. The remaining carbon is measured as NPOC, which for most
natural waters is operationally equivalent to DOC when the sample has
been filtered through 0.45 µm [@apha2012, Section 5310B].

For instrument operation, startup, and shutdown, see
[SOP-L204 Shimadzu TOC-L](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd). For
water-extractable DOC from soils, see
[SOP-L418](SOP-L418-water-extractable-doc.qmd).


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Filtered (0.45 µm) water samples from surface water,
  groundwater, stormwater, effluent, and precipitation, analyzed for
  DOC in NPOC mode on the Shimadzu TOC-L
- **Does not apply to:** Total organic carbon in unfiltered water (use
  TOC mode on the TOC-L); particulate organic carbon (requires
  separate filtration and combustion); soil carbon by SSM (see
  [SOP-L407](SOP-L407-total-carbon.qmd)); soil extract DOC (see
  [SOP-L418](SOP-L418-water-extractable-doc.qmd)); microbial biomass
  carbon (see [SOP-L409](SOP-L409-microbial-biomass-carbon.qmd))
- **Location:** EA Program analytical laboratory, SGM 133

| Instrument Manager | Maintain the TOC-L per [SOP-L204](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd) |
| Trained Personnel  | Prepare samples and standards, run analysis, export data |
| New Students       | Complete training before independent use               |


## Definitions

- **Calibration blank:** Deionized water (18.2 MΩ·cm) of verified DOC
  less than 0.05 mg C/L; used as the zero point for calibration and
  as the system blank to verify background carbon from the instrument
  and reagents.
- **CCV (continuing calibration verification):** A mid-range KHP
  standard analyzed at regular intervals during an analytical run to
  confirm calibration stability; acceptance criterion is 90--110%
  recovery; if outside this range, re-calibrate and re-run affected
  samples [@apha2012].
- **Chromophoric dissolved organic matter (CDOM):** The fraction of
  DOC that absorbs UV/visible light; derived primarily from aromatic
  humic and fulvic acids; a surrogate indicator of DOC concentration
  in optically characterized waters [@thurman1985].
- **Dissolved organic carbon (DOC):** Organic carbon that passes
  through a 0.45 µm filter; in natural waters, DOC includes humic
  substances, fulvic acids, amino acids, carbohydrates, and other
  soluble organic compounds; the operationally defined quantity
  measured as NPOC by the Shimadzu TOC-L [@thurman1985; @apha2012].
- **Field blank:** A sample of deionized water processed through the
  field collection equipment (bottles, filters, cooler) and returned
  to the laboratory for analysis; used to detect contamination
  introduced during sample collection and transport [@sharp1993].
- **Humic substances:** High-molecular-weight, polydisperse aromatic
  compounds derived from the decomposition of plant and microbial
  material; typically comprise 40--80% of DOC in natural fresh waters
  [@thurman1985].
- **IC (inorganic carbon):** Carbon present as dissolved CO~2~,
  bicarbonate (HCO~3~^-^), and carbonate (CO~3~^2-^); removed from
  water samples by acidification and sparging before NPOC measurement.
- **KHP (potassium hydrogen phthalate, KC~8~H~5~O~4~):** The primary
  calibration standard for TOC analysis; a pure, non-hygroscopic
  organic acid weighed accurately to prepare standards of known carbon
  concentration; 1.0000 g KHP = 0.4711 g C.
- **Method blank:** Deionized water acidified and processed identically
  to field samples, including any filtration and preservation steps;
  used to detect contamination from reagents and equipment; must read
  less than 0.2 mg C/L [@apha2012].
- **NPOC (non-purgeable organic carbon):** The organic carbon
  remaining in a sample after acidification (typically with HCl or
  H~3~PO~4~) and sparging with carrier gas to remove IC and volatile
  organic carbon (VOC); the quantity reported as DOC by the Shimadzu
  TOC-L [@apha2012, Section 5310B].
- **Particulate organic carbon (POC):** Organic carbon retained on a
  0.45 µm filter; not measured by this SOP; requires separate filter
  collection and combustion analysis.
- **Pre-combusted glass vial:** A TOC autosampler vial heated to
  450 °C for at least 4 hours to destroy residual organic carbon from
  the glass or manufacturing process; used to prevent contamination of
  samples from the container.
- **PVDF (polyvinylidene fluoride) filter:** A 0.45 µm syringe filter
  with low organic carbon leaching; preferred for DOC sample
  filtration; cellulose acetate filters must not be used because they
  leach DOC [@kaplan1994].
- **TOC (total organic carbon):** The sum of DOC and POC; in this SOP,
  only DOC (the filtered, NPOC fraction) is measured.


## Safety and Hazards

All safety requirements from
[SOP-L204](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd) Section 4 apply.

Additional hazards specific to this method:

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Hydrochloric acid (2 M HCl) is used for sample
  acidification and preservation. Avoid skin and eye contact.
- **Glassware:** Pre-combusted glass vials are fragile. Handle with
  care to avoid cuts.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves


## Required Materials

### Equipment

| Item                                  | Notes                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Shimadzu TOC-L with ASI-L autosampler | Operated per [SOP-L204](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd) |
| TNM-L (optional)                      | If simultaneous TN analysis is desired |
| Vacuum filtration apparatus           | Per [SOP-L114](SOP-L114-vacuum-filtration.qmd) |
| Analytical balance (0.001 g)          | Per [SOP-L200](SOP-L200-analytical-balance-calibration.qmd) |

### Consumables

| Item                                       | Notes                          |
|:-------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Pre-combusted glass vials (40 mL, PTFE-lined caps) | Combust at 450 °C for 4 hours per [SOP-L111](SOP-L111-muffle-furnace.qmd) |
| Autosampler vials (8 mL or 40 mL)         | Pre-combusted or acid-washed   |
| 0.45 µm filters (PVDF or PES)             | Do NOT use cellulose acetate [@kaplan1994] |
| Syringe filters (0.45 µm, 25 mm, PVDF)    | Discard first 2--3 mL of filtrate |

### Reagents

| Reagent                               | Notes                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| KHP stock standard (1000 mg C/L)     | 2.125 g KHP per 1 L DI water; prepare fresh monthly; store at 4 °C [@apha2012] |
| 2 M HCl (Trace Metal grade)          | For sample acidification and preservation |
| Deionized water (18.2 MΩ·cm)         | Verify DOC less than 0.05 mg/L before each session |

::: {.callout-important}
Prepare the 1000 mg C/L KHP stock fresh monthly or verify against a
certified reference material (CRM) before use. Degraded stock causes
a systematic low bias across the calibration.
:::


## Sample Collection and Preservation

Proper sample handling is critical; contamination from fingers, plastic
containers, and atmospheric CO~2~ can bias results [@sharp1993].

- Collect samples in pre-combusted glass bottles. Do not use plastic
  bottles for DOC samples.
- Filter through 0.45 µm PVDF syringe filters within 4 hours of
  collection; discard the first 2--3 mL of filtrate.
- Acidify filtered samples to pH ≤ 2 with 2 M HCl (approximately
  100 µL per 40 mL sample) to suppress microbial activity.
- Store acidified samples at 4 °C in the dark; analyze within 28 days
  [@apha2012].
- Cap vials immediately after filling to minimize atmospheric CO~2~
  contamination.


## Procedure

### Calibration

Prepare a 5-point calibration curve in the expected sample
concentration range [@apha2012]:

| Level | Concentration (mg C/L) | Preparation               |
|:------|:-----------------------|:--------------------------|
| 0     | 0.00                   | Acidified DI water blank  |
| 1     | 0.50                   | Dilute from 1000 mg/L KHP |
| 2     | 1.00                   | Dilute from 1000 mg/L KHP |
| 3     | 5.00                   | Dilute from 1000 mg/L KHP |
| 4     | 10.00                  | Dilute from 1000 mg/L KHP |
| 5     | 25.00                  | Dilute from 1000 mg/L KHP |

Adjust the range to match expected sample concentrations. Load
standards into pre-combusted autosampler vials and enter into the
Sample Table in LabSolutions TOC.

### Setting Up the Sample Table

1. Open LabSolutions TOC and start a new analysis.
2. Enter calibration standards (type = Standard), blanks (type =
   Blank), CCV standards, and samples.
3. Set the measurement mode to **NPOC** for all samples and blanks.
4. Set the number of injections per sample to 3; the software reports
   the mean and coefficient of variation (CV).
5. Enter dilution factors for any samples that have been diluted
   before the run.

### Running the Analysis

1. Load all vials into the autosampler; verify rack positions match
   the Sample Table.
2. Confirm the ASI-L rinse reservoir is full.
3. Click **Start** and monitor the first few injections for normal
   peak shape and baseline stability.
4. The run proceeds unattended; the autosampler advances automatically.

### Data Review and Export

1. After the run, open the Data Browser.
2. Check each result:
   - Replicate injection CV must be less than 2%.
   - Blank values must be less than 0.1 mg C/L.
   - CCV recovery must be 90--110%; re-calibrate and re-run affected
     samples if outside this range.
3. Dilute and re-run any sample exceeding the calibration range.
4. Export results to CSV per [SOP-L204](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd)
   Section 7.9.
5. Record the run in the instrument logbook.


## Calculations

The TOC-L software reports NPOC concentration directly in mg C/L,
corrected for dilution factor if entered in the Sample Table. Report
as DOC:

$$
\text{DOC (mg C/L)} = \text{NPOC}_{\text{reported}} - \text{NPOC}_{\text{method blank}}
$$

If samples were diluted before analysis, apply the dilution factor:

$$
\text{DOC (mg C/L)} = (\text{NPOC}_{\text{reported}} - \text{NPOC}_{\text{blank}}) \times D
$$

where $D$ is the dilution factor.

### R Code for Batch Processing


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# SOP-L311: DOC (NPOC) -- batch calculation from TOC-L CSV export
raw <- read.csv("TOC-L_export.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

blanks <- raw[grepl("^Blank|^DI|^MQ", raw$SampleID, ignore.case = TRUE), ]
ccv    <- raw[grepl("^CCV|^CVS|^Check", raw$SampleID, ignore.case = TRUE), ]

mean_blank <- mean(blanks$NPOC_mg_L, na.rm = TRUE)
cat(sprintf("Mean method blank: %.3f mg C/L\n", mean_blank))

samples <- raw[!grepl("^Blank|^DI|^MQ|^CCV|^CVS|^Check|^Std",
                       raw$SampleID, ignore.case = TRUE), ]
samples$DOC_mg_L <- (samples$NPOC_mg_L - mean_blank) * samples$Dilution
samples$DOC_mg_L[samples$DOC_mg_L < 0] <- 0
samples$QC_flag <- ifelse(samples$CV_pct > 2, "CV>2%", "")

print(samples[, c("SampleID", "NPOC_mg_L", "Dilution", "DOC_mg_L", "QC_flag")],
      row.names = FALSE)
```
:::



## Quality Control

### Instrument QC

Per [SOP-L204](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd):

- System blank less than 0.1 mg C/L
- Calibration $r^2 \geq 0.999$
- Replicate injection CV less than 2%
- CCV recovery 90--110%

### Method QC

| QC Element               | Frequency            | Acceptance Criteria            |
|:-------------------------|:---------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Method blank             | 1 per batch          | Less than 0.2 mg C/L           |
| Field blank              | 1 per sampling event | Less than 0.5 mg C/L           |
| Laboratory duplicate     | 1 per 10 samples     | RPD less than 10%              |
| CRM (when available)     | 1 per batch          | Recovery 90--110%              |
| Matrix spike             | 1 per 20 samples     | Recovery 80--120%              |

### Common Contamination Sources

| Source                       | Prevention                                |
|:-----------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Fingers touching vial interiors | Always wear gloves; handle by exterior only |
| Cellulose acetate filters    | Use PVDF or PES filters exclusively [@kaplan1994] |
| Detergent residue on glassware | Pre-combust glass; acid-wash and rinse with DI |
| Atmospheric CO~2~ absorption | Minimize headspace; cap immediately       |
| Degraded DI water            | Verify DI DOC less than 0.05 mg/L before each session |
| Old or degraded KHP stock    | Prepare fresh monthly; refrigerate        |


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                 | Disposal Method                               |
|:---------------------------|:----------------------------------------------|
| Acidified sample waste     | Neutralize and drain, or collect per [SOP-L006](SOP-L006-waste-disposal.qmd) |
| Calibration standard waste | Drain (dilute KHP, non-hazardous)             |
| Used syringe filters       | Standard trash                                |
| Pre-combusted glass vials  | Rinse and reuse, or glass recycling           |

## Training Record

Before performing this analysis independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete instrument training per
   [SOP-L204](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd) Section 14
3. Demonstrate competence preparing KHP calibration standards
4. Demonstrate proper sample filtration technique (PVDF filter,
   first-rinse discard)
5. Run a complete batch (calibration, blanks, CCV, samples) under
   supervision with acceptable QC results
6. Be signed off by the PI or instrument manager
